newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms on reserve data, interbank steady.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms on reserve data, interbank steady.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed late on Thursday as the market reacted to higher than expected June foreign reserve figures announced by the central bank this afternoon, dealers said.

In the onshore market the baht was quoted at 31.75/31.90 against 32.07/32.17 this morning after the central bank announced foreign reserves in June fell to $32.4 billion, from $33.3 billion a month earlier.
The decline was less than many had expected given central bank intervention against baht speculators in the run up to the currency's de facto devaluation on July 2, they said.
"I think the market was waiting for the BOT to have sold more reserves and the figure was better than expected," said a dealer at a local bank.
Limited month end covering also helped the baht, they said.
But the dollar remained well-bid by Thai banks buying for corporate clients and some dealers were surprised the economic data failed to make more impact.

"Given the figures came out encouraging, I personally thought the baht would strengthen further, but it's really amazing the amount local banks have been covering for their corporates," said another spot dealer.
The one month baht/dollar swap premium was offered at 13/18 satang per dollar.
Liquidity was unchanged from the morning with the interbank overnight offered rate at 12-16 percent.
But overnight lending continued to be confined among the stronger local financial institutions, dealers said.
